title: Probabilistic change-point canary gate with context-weighted KDE
author: Aisha N. Patel
release_notes: Add new probabilistic change-point (PCP) detector as an optional rollout guard. Improves detection of subtle latency/throughput regressions by combining kernel density estimation with contextual weighting and temporal smoothing. Backward compatible with existing canary pipelines. Default off for customers; opt-in via canary profile.
description: Motivation: Existing threshold and percentile-based canary checks miss gradual or context-dependent regressions that manifest as subtle distributional shifts. This PR introduces a probabilistic change-point (PCP) canary gate that detects distributional changes in latency and throughput by estimating recent and baseline densities with kernel density estimation (KDE), applying context weights (traffic shape, request size, model variant), and deriving a probabilistic change score used by the rollout controller. Design/changes: 1) New detector module canary/detectors/pcp_detector.py implemented in Python; it exposes a Detector interface compatible with the canary runner. 2) Lightweight Go adapter in canary/orchestrator/runner.go wires the detector into the existing canary evaluation flow and emits structured telemetry. 3) New default_canary_profiles.yaml contains an opt-in profile: pcp-sensitive with tunable window sizes, kernel bandwidth scheduler, and alpha thresholds for automated soft/hard rollback. 4) Telemetry: metrics/labels added to metrics_registry.yaml and dashboards/pcp_canary_overview.json for visual inspection. 5) Tests: deterministic unit tests for KDE behavior, synthetic integration tests that inject controlled shifts (e2e-tests/pcp_canary_integration.test), and bench scripts for profiling. 6) Docs and runbook: docs/pcp_canary.md and runbooks/perf_canary_pcp.md outline tuning guidance and incident playbook. Implementation notes: The detector computes two KDEs (baseline and probe) using Gaussian kernels with an adaptive bandwidth based on Silverman's rule scaled by traffic variance per-context. Context weights come from a routing key (model_id, request_size_bucket, priority) and are applied to reweight samples before density estimation; this reduces false positives when traffic composition changes. A Bayesian change probability is computed by comparing log-likelihoods and calibrated using historical false-positive windows. The detector emits a change_score [0..1], a p_value, and a representative fingerprint sample. Integration and rollback policy: The canary controller now supports a three-tier response: monitor-only (log/metric), soft-rollback (throttle new traffic routes to control plane fallback), and hard-rollback (immediate traffic switch and alert). The profile configuration maps change_score thresholds to actions and cooldowns. Performance and safety: Microbenchmarks on a 64-node testbed with synthetic load show median detector CPU of ~12ms/sample and <2% added end-to-end canary latency for typical 5s evaluation windows. We added a sampling rate cap and a batched estimator path for high-throughput customers to limit overhead. Backwards compatibility: Detector registers behind the existing abstraction with the new profile disabled by default; existing linear and percentile checks are unchanged. How to test locally: run perf-canary/Makefile targets test-pcp and bench-pcp; e2e test harness can simulate controlled drift using scripts/bench/poc_latency_profile.py. Rollout plan: feature behind opt-in profile for 2 weeks in canary orgs, then gradually enable as default for internal smoke accounts if FPR < 0.5% over 14 days. Observability/alerts: New alerts perf_canary_pcp_high_probable_change and perf_canary_pcp_consistent_shift for sustained changes; dashboards added. Security/privacy: detector only uses aggregated latencies and metadata keys; no PII. Documentation: detailed tuning guidance and example Linear tasks are included. Related work: complements percentile-decay and traffic-shape guards by capturing distributional shifts. Summary: Adds a robust probabilistic change-point detector with context weighting, integrated into canary orchestration with safe rollout controls and observability.

notes_for_ops: Ops: New alerts added; to quiet noisy signals during initial rollout set profile.pcp.sensitivity=low. For high-throughput orgs enable batched_estimator and sample_rate<=0.1; verify metrics perf_canary.pcp_change_probability and perf_canary.pcp_fingerprint_count in dashboards.
bench_results_summary: Local bench (simulated 1k rps): detector median CPU 12ms/sample; batched estimator reduces CPU to ~3ms/sample at 10k rps. Canary evaluation latency impact <2% for 5s windows under test. See scripts/bench output in artifacts for detailed numbers.
test_instructions: Run make test-pcp (unit + integration). For e2e, run e2e-tests/pcp_canary_integration.test with --inject-shift magnitude=0.15 and validate that change_score exceeds configured thresholds in logs/metrics.
